chunks: And through this chain of narrators from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: He informed us that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Matil informed him from his uncle, Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Matil, who said: When death approached Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari (may Allah be pleased with him), I was sitting near his head, asking him questions and conversing with him, while Abu al-Qasim ibn Ruh was near his feet. He turned to me and said: 'I have been ordered to bequeave my affairs to Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh.' He said: 'So I rose from his head side, took the hand of Abu al-Qasim, seated him in my place, and moved to sit at his feet.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ رُوحٍ: Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, another Special Emissary
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari, a key figure among the Special Emissaries

ai.seo_question: How did the authority of the Special Emissaries transfer during the Minor Occultation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the formal succession of Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh as the fourth and final Special Emissary (*al-Na'ib al-Khas*) of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari. The scene, set during the Prophet's Peace be upon him's final illness, underscores the continuity of divine guidance through a structured chain of authority (*isnad*) during the Minor Occultation (*al-Ghayb al-Sughra*). It serves as a critical historical anchor for the Shia belief in the Imam's hidden presence and his delegated representatives.
